title: A history-range test found no clear departure in 20 plant transplant gradients
abstract: We tested whether plant communities exceeded the range of their first warmed state and all measured destination controls. This range is required by species-specific nonnegative first-order adjustment if targets stay inside measured limits. We used 40 contrasts in 20 TransPlant gradients and a conservative held-out plot-history score. Relative cover exceeded current controls: score 0.0225, with 95% cluster limits 0.0057 to 0.0403. The historical score was 0.0116, with limits -0.0075 to 0.0317. Occurrence and absolute cover also gave no clear historical departure. Country weights and two-gradient omission kept this uncertainty. Thus current-endpoint evidence does not reject this wider range. The result does not show that target history explains departures or that a lag model is valid. Small plot samples, range widening, shared blocks and unmeasured targets between censuses limit the test. We provide the bound, code, aggregate evidence, simulations and external-data retrieval instructions. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Conservative held-out range scores. Positive expected scores exceed the tested range. Error bars show 95% study-cluster bootstrap limits. Negative scores do not establish a lag model.

citations.reason: Tests its open changing-target limitation using a wider historical range and a different conservative score.
